title: Spatial index of urban environment for health
author: Mara Lucia Marques
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb3jiqkn

steps.title: Collect Demographic and Environmental Data
steps.instruction: Gather the necessary spatial and demographic data for the study area (e.g., Jataí, Goiás, Brazil).

substeps.instruction: Obtain population data per sector to determine population density (people/km2) using IBGE (2011) sources.
Collect data on road connectivity and land use/vegetation cover to determine urban green space density (green m2/people) and road density (road km/km2) using SIEG (2018) sources.
Acquire urban area slope parameters using the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (MDE – SRTM) with a spatial resolution of 30 m (EMBRAPA, 1979).

steps.title: Calculate Spatial Urban Health Index (SUHI)
steps.instruction: Use a Geographic Information System (GIS) to compute the SUHI using the weighted multi-criteria overlay method.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a geographic database using ArcGIS 10.5.1 (ESRI v. 2018).
Apply the SUHI equation: SUHI = Dpopulation + Dgreen area + Slope + Droad connection.
Classify the resulting representativeness index (km2) into four gradation levels (from unfavorable to very favorable to physical activity) using the quantile method.
